_doc: schemaVersion 2 (#390) added `effect`: the plain-language statement of what the pick MECHANICALLY does, written in the same declaration as the lever it describes so the two cannot drift. `flavor` is who you were; `effect` is what it changes about the store.

backstories.label: Ex-Mechanic
backstories.flavor: Years in the shop taught you what corners get cut. You spot a blown head gasket before anyone else does.
backstories.effect: You read a car better than the people you buy from, so fewer of your units hide a repair bill you never budgeted for.

backstories.label: Ex-Banker
backstories.flavor: You know how money moves. Your former employer extended a personal line of credit as a parting gift.
backstories.effect: A $50,000 line of credit stands behind the store, there to draw on when a slow week empties the account.

backstories.label: Inheritor
backstories.flavor: You got the keys — and the debts, the grudges, and the regulars who remember your father.
backstories.effect: You open with $25,000 more cash than anyone else, but the town remembers your father, so fewer people walk in until you have won them back.
